source.name: Forward-delay explanation
source.html:
Other delay structures can be represented within this subset:

  • Forward delays.

notes: These constructions identify a subset: delays occur in feedback loops, with one delay in each loop. This describes the form of the model we build. It does not mean that the original design must already have this appearance.

For example, a forward delay can be expressed using a feedback construction. The output retrieves the stored value, while the current input supplies the next stored value. It therefore preserves the intended one-reaction delay. Trace the input/output and state paths. State equivalence assumes the corresponding initial value; do not skip initialisation when comparing behaviours.

This is the same construction expressed using the interfaces we just introduced: get and set, together with the composition operations. Point out the correspondence after the Morph settles. Do not reread the whole signature from P15.

A loop containing several delays can also be represented. Here the two-delay example first exposes one delay in the forward path, then uses the previous construction to express it. The resulting structure has one delay per loop, while retaining the original stored information and behaviour. Follow the bottom drawings left to right. Do not describe two delays as one total register. These are equivalent synchronous representations with corresponding initial states, not a hardware-cost or latency optimisation or permission for arbitrary zero-delay feedback. Transition: We have described how to connect components and thread their state. Next, we need specifications of the components’ intended behaviour.

Presenter guidance: P17 introduces component contracts; P18 addresses reasoning across a language boundary; the rising-pattern example follows on P19.
